title: Practice: Balancing Chemical Equations
description: Low-stakes practice on coefficients, subscripts, atom counting, and balancing simple chemical equations.

questions.question: When balancing a chemical equation, which part may you change?
questions.explanation: Balancing changes coefficients only. Changing subscripts or symbols changes the substances in the reaction.

questions.question: How many hydrogen atoms are represented by 2H2O?
questions.explanation: Each H2O molecule has 2 hydrogen atoms. The coefficient 2 means there are two water molecules, so 2 x 2 = 4 hydrogen atoms.

questions.question: True or False: A missing coefficient in front of a formula means the coefficient is 1.
questions.explanation: True. If no coefficient is written, one particle or formula unit is understood.

questions.question: True or False: Changing H2O to H2O2 is an acceptable way to balance oxygen atoms when water is the product.
questions.explanation: False. H2O is water and H2O2 is hydrogen peroxide. Changing a subscript changes the substance.

questions.question: Fill in the missing coefficient: __ H2 + O2 -> 2H2O
questions.explanation: The products contain 4 hydrogen atoms in 2H2O, so the reactant side needs 2H2.

questions.question: Balance the equation: Mg + O2 -> MgO
questions.explanation: O2 has 2 oxygen atoms, so place 2 before MgO. Then place 2 before Mg to balance magnesium.

questions.question: Which equation is balanced?
questions.explanation: N2 + 3H2 -> 2NH3 has 2 nitrogen atoms and 6 hydrogen atoms on both sides.

questions.question: In one or two sentences, explain why subscripts should not be changed when balancing chemical equations.
questions.correctAnswer: Subscripts should not be changed because they are part of the chemical formula and determine the identity of the substance. Balancing should change only coefficients.
questions.explanation: A subscript tells how many atoms are in one particle of a substance. Changing it creates a different substance instead of balancing the original reaction.
